subject: Security: evidence transfer window request and retention-exception coordination
messages:
From: Samuel Park <samuel.park@finhaven.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-security@finhaven.com, FinHaven Legal <legal@finhaven.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: IR evidence request + retention exception for suspected data exposure

Marissa —

Quick heads up: we detected a suspicious export from one of our integrations that may have included a small set of customer IDs and obfuscated tokens. We are still investigating but need to request your IR plan and a short-term retention exception to preserve logs beyond our normal 90‑day window while we validate scope.

What we need from Redwood immediately:
- Confirmation of an evidence transfer window (SFTP/preferred method) within the next 48 hours
- A copy of your incident response plan (SOC2-aligned IR runbook) and any SOC 2 / SIG mapping that explains controls for tenant data access
- Guidance on redaction/sanitization expectations for logs you share back to us

We’ve attached a small CSV with indicators and example request IDs that triggered the alert. We appreciate this being prioritized — our legal and ops-security teams are on the thread.

Attachments: indicator-log-extract.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Samuel Park
Head of Security Operations
FinHaven
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Park <samuel.park@finhaven.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: IR evidence request + retention exception for suspected data exposure

Samuel —

Thanks for the alert and the sample extract. We’ll treat this as high priority. High-level plan from our side:

1) Acknowledge receipt and open an internal IR ticket (I’ve done this and assigned oncall).
2) Hold a 48‑hour evidence transfer window starting as soon as both sides confirm schedule — we can accept SFTP or an encrypted upload to a temporary Drive folder.
3) Share a sanitized copy of our IR playbook and a SIG/CAIQ crosswalk for the SOC 2 controls that map to tenant access and logging.
4) If you require retention beyond our standard 90 days, please send a formal retention-exception request (legal sign-off). We’ll fast-track approval steps where reasonable.

I attached a version of our IR playbook (redacted for public consumption) and a short checklist for sanitization. Kar is looped for telemetry extracts; Neha will own compliance/attestations and Jonas will be the legal contact for any retention exception.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Confirm SFTP or Drive and a preferred 2‑hour slot tomorrow between 09:00–16:00 PST
- If retaining logs beyond 90 days, please send legal request to legal@finhaven.com (we’ll need sign-off)

We’ll prepare the evidence packaging and share a manifest ahead of the handoff.

Attachments: [Attachment: ir_playbook_v2.pdf (pdf)], [Attachment: sanitization-guidelines.pdf (pdf)]

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Park <samuel.park@finhaven.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-14T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: IR evidence request + retention exception for suspected data exposure

Samuel / team —

Quick technical note from infra: we can produce granular request logs (application request id, originating IP, timestamps, and KV cache hit/miss metadata) and will apply a sanitize filter to remove PII before export. To align expectations:

- Typical export set for this scenario is ~12–24 hours of rolling request traces plus related auth logs. If you want broader coverage (7 days), let us know (size and redaction needs will change).
- We recommend an encrypted SFTP (user-scoped key) for transfer. We’ll provide a manifest and SHA256 sums.
- Sanitize plan: mask tokens, remove full user names, replace email addresses with hashes. See attached sanitization-guidelines.pdf for specifics.

If FinHaven can confirm the exact request IDs of interest and preferred window, we’ll stage the bundle and open an SFTP user. Also — if you sign the DocuSign retention-exception envelope Marissa referenced, that covers the temporary holding period and access audit requirements.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Lead, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Samuel Park <samuel.park@finhaven.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-security@finhaven.com, FinHaven Legal <legal@finhaven.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T16:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: IR evidence request + retention exception for suspected data exposure

Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the playbook. We reviewed the sanitization guidelines and confirm SFTP is preferred. We’ve completed the DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.example.com/envelope/0fc9-AB12 — legal will countersign by EOD.

Please schedule the SFTP window tomorrow 09:00–11:00 PST and send the SFTP credentials to ops-security@finhaven.com. We’ll provide the final list of request IDs by 08:00 PST tomorrow. Once upload completes we’ll validate checksums and confirm receipt.

On a separate note — could Redwood share the SOC 2 control IDs that correspond to your access logging and key management (we can reconcile against our SIG matrix later in the week).

Appreciate the help.

Samuel Park
Head of Security Operations
FinHaven
